title: Sparse Telemetry Approval Sandbox — PRD draft
summary: Draft PRD for an opt-in sandbox feature that reduces audit-volume and customer operational burden by enabling sparse telemetry sampling, short-lived approval sandboxes, and a forensic proof package that ties approval gates to customer-managed network attestations. Focused on Private deployments where customers prefer to control telemetry egress and want predictable approval latency for network changes.
goals: Provide an approval gate model that balances low operational overhead for customers with sufficient forensic data for post-change audits.
Allow customers to run ‘sandboxed’ network changes with sampled telemetry so that approval latency stays low while preserving a verifiable audit trail.
Integrate customer-managed networking signals (syslog, flow logs, signed handshakes) into approval decisions without requiring full continuous telemetry upload.
Ship an end-to-end prototype that Redwood SREs and two pilot customers can use to validate metrics and usability within 8 weeks of kickoff.
non_goals: Not intended as the final, fully audited enterprise retention pipeline — this is an opt-in sandbox and experiment phase.
Not replacing existing full-fidelity audit pipelines for high-compliance customers (FISMA/PCI/…); those will continue to use full exports.
Not a replacement for customer SIEM integrations; we provide a lightweight handoff and evidence package that can be consumed by SIEMs.
Not introducing new persistent plaintext egress of raw syslog into Redwood-controlled buckets in this phase.
requirements: R1: Approval Gate API that accepts a change bundle and returns allow/deny/pending with a human-readable rationale.
R2: Telemetry Sampling Config: per-customer policy allowing rate-limited sampling (examples: 1%, 100 events/min, prefix-based sampling).
R3: Forensic Proof Package: signed snapshot of request, sampled telemetry snippets, and timestamps; package signed by customer KMS or signed handshake when available.
R4: Local Buffering & Retry: customer-managed edge should buffer sampled telemetry for up to 24h if connectivity to Redwood control plane is down, with integrity checks on replay.
R5: Approval Latency SLO: median approval within 2 minutes, P95 <= 6 minutes for sandboxed flows when telemetry is available.
R6: Opt-in Consent Flow in Console: enable/disable sampling, configure retention window (24h–90d), and select evidence-level (minimal/standard/forensic).
R7: Minimal Data Surface: sampled telemetry must be redacted for PII by default, with higher evidence levels requiring explicit customer consent and KMS-backed encryption.
user_stories: As a Platform Engineer at AcmeCorp, I want to run a VPC rule change in a sandbox and receive an approval decision within minutes so I can validate behavior without affecting production.
As a Security Auditor for a regulated customer, I want to retrieve the forensic proof package for a change so I can validate who authorized it and what network signals were observed.
As a Redwood SRE, I want sampled telemetry to include correlation IDs and timing so we can reproduce observed approval latencies in our incident runbooks.
As a Customer Networking Lead, I want to limit telemetry upload rates to avoid bandwidth and storage costs while still keeping an auditable trail for rollbacks.
success_metrics: At least two pilot customers complete a sandbox change workflow end-to-end within 60 days of prototype release.
Average approval latency for sandbox flows <= 2 minutes (measured across pilot customers).
Forensic proof packages retrieved and validated by auditors for 100% of sandboxed changes sampled at 10% rate during pilot.
No customer-reported PII leakage incidents during sandbox pilot (0 incidents).
design_sketch: High-level: (1) Customer submits change bundle to Redwood control plane. (2) Control plane evaluates policy + available sampled telemetry handshakes. (3) If evidence sufficient, gate returns allow; otherwise return pending and request additional ephemeral evidence. (4) For every decision, create a signed forensic package stored (encrypted) in customer-designated storage or Redwood short-term store with explicit retention. Sampling rules determine which telemetry slices are included.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Week 0–2): Internal prototype — implement sampling config, basic approval API, and proof package format. Test with synthetic edge simulator.
Phase 1 (Week 3–6): Redwood-internal SRE dogfooding with two internal teams; gather latency and retention metrics.
Phase 2 (Week 7–12): Pilot with 2 external customers (opt-in) — monitor metrics, validate KMS signing handshakes, and collect auditor feedback.
Phase 3 (Post-pilot): Iterate on UI and evidence levels, prepare GA readiness checklist (security review, retention guarantees, SLA language).
Fallback: If telemetry unavailable, system falls back to conservative policy (deny or require manual approval) according to customer-configured tolerance.
privacy_and_security_considerations: Default redaction of IP addresses and user-agent strings in sampled telemetry; customers can opt-in to less-redacted evidence under tighter contractual terms.
Forensic packages are signed and optionally encrypted with customer KMS — Redwood only holds ciphertext when requested by the customer.
Retention windows configurable per-customer; short-term sandbox evidence kept no longer than 30 days unless explicitly archived.
Access controls: only authorized auditor roles with audit-justification headers can retrieve forensic packages; all retrievals logged.
Replay protection: replayed telemetry must carry monotonic counters and signature verification to prevent tampering.
operational_impacts: Increased control-plane storage for short-term packages; estimate 50–200MB/week per pilot customer at 10% sampling of metadata-only evidence.
Need for edge SDK changes to support signed handshakes and buffering/replay semantics.
SRE playbook additions for approval-decision debugging and forensic-package verification steps.
Support burden: initial onboarding runbooks and sample scripts for customer KMS integration and console enrollment.
open_questions: Q1: What exact format should the forensic package use to maximize SIEM compatibility (CEF, JSON-LD, compact protobuf)?
Q2: Should sampled telemetry include raw flow data or only headers and deltas for privacy?
Q3: What is the expected cost model for customers who opt into higher-evidence levels (bandwidth + storage pricing)?
Q4: How do we reconcile customer-managed retention policies with Redwood incident investigation needs?
Q5: Which customers should be eligible for the pilot (criteria: network size, compliance profile, dedicated account manager)?
appendix_notes: Implementation notes and quick prototype checklist: 1) Define sampling DSL and UI surface (example presets). 2) Implement minimal proof package signer that can accept external KMS public key for envelope signatures. 3) Build a ‘sampler simulator’ to generate realistic telemetry slices for offline testing. 4) Draft legal language for opt-in telemetry and evidence-level SLAs.
